recipes.name: Acorn Squash
ingredients_raw: 1 medium acorn squash, halved and seeded

steps.text: Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C).
Place squash halves, cut-side down, on a baking sheet. Bake in the preheated oven until flesh begins to soften, about 30 to 45 minutes.

Remove squash from the oven and transfer one squash half, cut-side up, to a deep baking dish. Spoon butter and brown sugar into the cavity. Place remaining squash half, cut-side down, over top to seal.
Return to the oven and continue to bake until flesh is soft, 30 minutes.

raw_recipe.headline: Acorn Squash
raw_recipe.description: Acorn squash is baked with just butter and brown sugar until perfectly soft and tender, sweet, and buttery for a deliciously easy fall side dish.

review.reviewBody: This is the only way I've ever had squash but you can do it a quicker way. Cut it in half and seed it. Microwave on high for 5 minutes. Put about a tablespoon of butter in each have and spread it around on the top edges and inside. Litely sprinkle nutmeg all over and then about twice as much cinnamon. Follow it up with brown sugar (1-2T each half depending on how sweet you like it) and bake at 350 for about 20 minutes. Feel free to turn the oven off and keep the squash in there until the rest of your meal is done. You just can't miss with squash this way!

Very good, but excellent after adding an equal amount of salt to the sugar. (If you like Kettle Corn, you'll love this. It's not too sweet this way.) Also, since I HATE having to cut these darn things in half, I just bake them whole for about an hour at 375. Then they can be cut in half with a butter knife! I then broil for 5 minutes to melt the butter/sugar/salt mix.
Heat Acorn squash in microwave 1 minute before slicing it length-wise.

I make this all the time. Sometime I cook butter butternut squash along with the acorn squash and after they have cooked I scrap out the meat and mix them together. My family loves this combination. I also also add a 1/4 cup of dark molasses, dark brown sugar and butter and fry it in a cast iron pan on med heat till it is heated through.

Had cooked acorn squash only once before and did not care for it much. When I found this recipe, I thought...oh well, I have the squash...here goes. The recipe seemed too simple! 
To make it faster, I used the InstaPot, cooking the halves for 15 minutes, then released the pressure. So well done they almost fell apart, so I put the mashed flesh into a oven proof bowl, added 2 T brown sugar, about a T of butter and a t of coconut oil. Sprinked 1/2 t of cinnamon on top and warmed it while something else was cooking (not necessary if already warm enough) and we devoured it....delicious! Will make for Thanksgiving dinner.

I love the recipe. Tried as is and loved it. Next time I caramelized some shallots and garlic then mixed in 1 Tablespoons of coconut sugar and 1 tablespoon of butter and a sprinkle of Cayenne pepper. And cooked as in the original recipe. Was amazing.

....delicious and simple Acorn Squash preparation. My little variation was to do the "second baking" with both sides apart ...flesh side up. I added the butter and brown sugar ...along with 1 tsp of bourbon to each of the halves ...and baked for 20 minutes covered with foil ...then increased the oven to 425 degrees and baked uncovered for the final 10 minutes. I got a nice browning and carmelization of the sugar on the upper lip of the squash.

This could not have been any easier! I think mine was done earlier than an hour, but I left it in for the full hour. Do yourself a favor and put a piece of parchment on your baking sheet before baking the last 30 minutes to make cleanup a breeze. Also, after 30 minutes of baking, I scored the inside of the squash before adding the butter and brown sugar, to help absorb the flavors. Thanks for sharing your recipe!

Only changes I made were method (5-6 minutes in the microwave, then 20 minutes in oven) and amounts of butter and sugar. I used 1 tsp. of butter in each half and had a pool of melted butter; I can't imagine a tablespoon per half! I used much less brown sugar too. As a kid, this was pretty much the only way we ate acorn squash. Thanks for the delicious memory! Will definitely make again.

I may use the basics for other squashes. I did change because of a 'kettle corn' comment from another member. I added 2T. salt and used 1 1/2T. butter, melted and mixed with the 2T. sugar. I flipped both halves and brushed the butter mix up the inside, the edges and where thee skin had separated. Then both were covered with a parchment disk and then foil to secure. Baked for another 23 minutes. Amazing. Thank you.
i cut mine in half and added the brown sugar, butter and raisins. the raisins are really good in this. i added about 1/2 or more of water in the dish around the squash. always turns out great

I personally am not a squash lover...but I came here to try and find a good recipe for Acorn Squash. OMG MY HUSBAND LOVES IT. I made it last night and he came home with a few more acorns. Asked me to make it again tonight.
It just has to work. Thank you for the accuracy
This was so easy and very good
Thinking I like butternut or honey nut better.

I love this easy recipe. I added 1 step because I have difficulty cutting the acorn squash in halves. I put my squash in the microwave for one or two minutes, depending on its size, to soften it before cutting. Poking holes prior to microwaving is optional . Juices may drip from poked holes.
We all love this recipe. It's simple to make with only two ingredients. And it's delicious!
I make this with Libby’s Pumpkin Curry soup and then fill the squash with the soup. They are great together!!😊

You can eat this as a dessert with butter, brown sugar and cinnamon or as a meal with butter, onion, bacon and salt and pepper. I never heard of adding the step of cooking them upside down first though. If you put a small amount of butter around the edges when baking, they turn a beautiful brown.
Cinnamon was a great suggestion! I’ve never made acorn squash before but this was a delicious intro for sure
